cross_cutting_observations.structural_vs_value_positions: All 9 TP alerts inject into quoted VALUE literals (LIKE '{query}', WHERE value='{query}', WHERE conceptidfrom='{conceptid}') built by str.format/% into the full query text - classic value-position injection. The only structural-position interpolations flagged are operator-trust candidates (export.py FROM {0} table identifier; index_database.py CTE/IN-list interpolations produced no alerts this run). No ORDER BY or column-name interpolation from request data exists in the snapshot.
cross_cutting_observations.bound_parameter_barrier: The 44 reviewed execute(sql, params) sites (ETL, MVT, buffer, etc.) produced zero alerts, i.e. the parameter-binding barrier correctly suppressed all value-slot flows; every alert that fired involves single-argument execute(sql) of format/%-built text. No alert was found where a bound parameter was misreported as the query text.
cross_cutting_observations.guard_gap: get_child_edges validates conceptid via uuid.UUID (models/concept.py:502-506) but interpolates the original variable - a validation guard, not a transformation. CodeQL's barrier model does not prune it, producing alerts #2/#4/#5. In reality only UUID-alphabet strings (hex digits, hyphens, braces, urn:uuid: prefix - no quotes) survive the guard, so that slot is not injectable; the sink remains exploitable through the unguarded query parameter, which is what alerts #0/#1/#3 capture.
cross_cutting_observations.duplicate_encodings: 9 of the 23 alerts are duplicate sink-node encodings of the same 3 underlying TPs (construction call node vs. argument vs. execute call), yielding 3 distinct true-positive vulnerabilities from 9 TP alerts; the report's '23 raw / 0 auto-TP / 23 candidate' counts are consistent with this.
cross_cutting_observations.auth_verification: dropdown and paged_dropdown are registered in arches/urls.py:115-116 with no auth decorators (verified at the function definitions in views/concept.py:375/381); the JSON-LD import alternative path (alerts #2/#4/#5) requires user_can_edit_resource, further supporting its FP verdict.

real_vulnerability_hit_check.question: Were the two real CWE-89 vulnerabilities (fixed in upstream commit 7ed53e2, per the function data supplied in the review prompt) hit by the formal Pass 5 results?

functions.vulnerable_site: sql = sql.format(query=query.lower(), ...) at :424 followed by cursor.execute(sql) at :426 (matches code_before exactly)
functions.evidence: Alerts #9/#10/#11 report precisely the pre-fix code: request.GET.get("query") at :383 -> sql.format(query=...) at :424 -> cursor.execute(sql) at :426, on an unauthenticated route (/concepts/paged_dropdown). All three verdicts likely_tp (confidence 0.97). The post-fix version moves to %(query)s placeholders with a params dict - i.e. the alert flags exactly what the patch changed.
functions.note: The same request parameter also flows through get_child_collections_hierarchically(query=...) into get_child_edges' %-formatted LIKE subquery (alerts #0/#1/#3, models/concept.py:646/:635 -> :653 -> :723) - an additional genuinely vulnerable sink reached from the same vulnerable view, consistent with the multi-issue commit message (fixes #9019, #9021, #9026).

functions.vulnerable_site: sql = """... WHERE d.conceptidfrom = '{0}' ...""".format(conceptid) at :1180-1202 followed by cursor.execute(sql) at :1216 (matches code_before exactly)
functions.evidence: Alerts #6/#7/#8 trace request.GET.get("conceptid") (views/concept.py:376, unauthenticated route /concepts/dropdown) -> Concept().get_e55_domain(conceptid) (:377) -> .format(conceptid) (models/concept.py:1180-1202) -> cursor.execute(sql) (:1216). No uuid validation, no parameter binding - exactly the code the patch converted to cursor.execute(sql, [conceptid]) with %s. All three verdicts likely_tp (confidence 0.97).

real_vulnerability_hit_check.conclusion: 命中。Both real vulnerabilities in the supplied commit data were detected by the formal Pass 5 rule: paged_dropdown by alerts #9/#10/#11 (plus the related get_child_edges query-slot chain #0/#1/#3), and get_e55_domain by alerts #6/#7/#8. Both vulnerable code sites correspond line-for-line to the pre-fix code, both entry routes are unauthenticated, and both lack any parameter binding at the flagged sink. No genuine vulnerability in the supplied data was missed.
real_vulnerability_hit_check.caveat: The two other fix locations implied by the commit (issues #9019/#9021/#9026 beyond the two supplied functions) were not part of the prompt's function list and were not separately assessed against ground truth; the get_child_edges query-slot chain (alerts #0/#1/#3) covers the paged_dropdown data path regardless.
